section: Right to Information Act 2005 - structure, exemptions, amendments and issues
subsections: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology
Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty

accepted.s: Which enactment is associated with Sweden's pioneering recognition of freedom of information in 1766?
o: Administrative Procedure Act
Freedom of the Press Act
Official Secrets Act
Public Records Act
accepted.x: Sweden enacted the Freedom of the Press Act in 1766, regarded as the world's first freedom-of-information law.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact title associated with the landmark year.
accepted.sec: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights is significant in the context of the right to information because it recognises the right to
o: seek and receive information
participate in every legislative proceeding
free legal aid in all civil disputes
access confidential state records without restriction
accepted.x: UDHR Article 19, adopted in 1948, recognises the right to seek and receive information.
accepted.tq: Match the international instrument with the precise right it recognises.
accepted.sec: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The public hearings known as ‘jan sunwais’, involving muster rolls and bills, were central to the activities of which organisation?
o: Swaraj Abhiyan
People's Union for Civil Liberties
National Campaign for People's Right to Information
Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan
accepted.x: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan conducted jan sunwais in Rajasthan to demand access to muster rolls and bills, helping initiate the RTI movement.
accepted.tq: Link the distinctive activity with the organisation that conducted it.
accepted.sec: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains the principal leaders associated with the MKSS-led public hearings in Rajasthan?
o: Aruna Roy, Medha Patkar and Shankar Singh
Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh
Shankar Singh, Jayaprakash Narayan and Nikhil Dey
Nikhil Dey, Anna Hazare and Aruna Roy
accepted.x: The Rajasthan movement was associated with Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely associated public-activism names.
accepted.sec: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following earlier State-level right-to-information laws in chronological order:
A. Delhi
B. Rajasthan and Karnataka
C. Maharashtra and Assam
D. Tamil Nadu and Goa
o: D, B, A, C
B, D, A, C
D, A, B, C
B, A, D, C
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu and Goa enacted laws in 1997, Rajasthan and Karnataka in 2000, Delhi in 2001, and Maharashtra and Assam in 2002.
accepted.tq: Use the years attached to the state-level laws to fix the sequence.
accepted.sec: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the judicial basis of the right to information:
1. The right to know has been read into Article 19(1)(a).
2. Article 21 has also been associated with the judicial protection of the right to know.
3. State of U.P. v. Raj Narain and S.P. Gupta v. Union of India are important cases in this context.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The right to know has been judicially linked with Articles 19(1)(a) and 21. State of U.P. v. Raj Narain and S.P. Gupta v. Union of India are important decisions supporting this principle.
accepted.tq: Check the constitutional provisions and case-law references together.
accepted.sec: Background - Sweden, FOI Act, MKSS, first states - chronology  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the nature of the right created by the Right to Information Act, 2005?
o: It is merely an administrative privilege available at the discretion of each public authority.
It is a Fundamental Right expressly created by a separate constitutional article.
It is a statutory right, while the Supreme Court has read the right to know into Article 19(1)(a).
It is a constitutional right confined to citizens holding public office.
accepted.x: The Act creates a statutory right. Separately, the Supreme Court has treated the right to know as implicit in Article 19(1)(a).
accepted.tq: Separate the statutory source of the Act from its constitutional interpretation.

accepted.s: Under the Right to Information framework, information is provided free of cost to applicants belonging to which category?
o: All applicants below 25 years of age
Applicants who are government employees
All applicants belonging to rural areas
Persons below the poverty line
accepted.x: Applicants belonging to the below-poverty-line category are entitled to information without payment of the prescribed fee.
accepted.tq: Recall the specific beneficiary category attached to fee exemption.

accepted.s: The Preamble of the Right to Information Act seeks to promote an informed citizenry and transparency primarily in order to
o: contain corruption and hold governments accountable, while harmonising these objectives with other public interests
transfer all information-related functions from public authorities to courts
make every government document automatically public without exception
replace the parliamentary system with direct democracy
accepted.x: The Preamble connects informed citizenship and transparency with containing corruption and ensuring accountability, subject to harmonisation with other public interests.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that retains the complete purpose without an absolute claim.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Central and State Information Commissions:
1. Both are statutory bodies created under the Right to Information Act.
2. Both have powers of a civil court.
3. Both hear second appeals and complaints under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The Central and State Information Commissions are statutory bodies. They exercise civil-court powers and deal with second appeals and complaints under the Act.
accepted.tq: Verify the common features before considering the Central-State distinction.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to the composition of the Information Commissions, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Central and State Commissions may each consist of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
The State Commission has a Chief Information Commissioner and a maximum of five Information Commissioners.
Each Commission must consist of exactly ten Information Commissioners besides its Chief.
The Central Commission consists only of the Chief Information Commissioner, whereas the State Commission has up to ten members.
accepted.x: At both levels, the structure consists of a Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten Information Commissioners.
accepted.tq: Watch the difference between ‘up to’ and a compulsory fixed number.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a ground mentioned for removal of an Information Commissioner?
o: Disagreement with the decision of a Public Information Officer
Holding paid employment outside the office
Insolvency
Conviction for an offence involving moral turpitude
accepted.x: Removal may be connected with insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude, paid employment and other specified grounds. Mere disagreement with a PIO's decision is not a ground for removal.
accepted.tq: Find the option that is unrelated to the statutory removal grounds.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the ordinary procedure for removal of a Central Information Commissioner on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, which combination is correct?
o: The Chief Justice of India orders removal after an inquiry by the President.
The Prime Minister orders removal after an inquiry by Parliament.
The Governor orders removal after an inquiry by the High Court.
The President orders removal after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
accepted.x: For proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the President may remove a Central Information Commissioner after the Supreme Court conducts the required inquiry.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who would do this job?’ method for authority and inquiry.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding eligibility for appointment as an Information Commissioner is correct?
o: Only serving Members of Parliament and Members of Legislative Assemblies are eligible.
A person holding an office of profit is automatically eligible because the post is statutory.
A person connected with a political party is expressly preferred for appointment.
A person of eminence in public life with experience in fields such as law, science and technology, social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration may be appointed.
accepted.x: Eligibility requires eminence in public life and experience in specified fields. MPs and MLAs, persons holding an office of profit, and persons connected with political parties or business are ineligible.
accepted.tq: Select the inclusive eligibility statement while rejecting disqualifying conditions.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the post-2019 position regarding the tenure of Information Commissioners?
o: The Act continues to prescribe five years or the age of 65 years in all cases.
The Constitution fixes a uniform tenure of six years.
The concerned High Court fixes the tenure separately for each Commissioner.
The Central Government notifies the term; under the RTI Rules, 2019, it is three years.
accepted.x: After the 2019 amendment, the Central Government is empowered to notify the term. The RTI Rules, 2019 provide a three-year term.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original tenure provision from the post-2019 rule-based position.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who was the first Central Information Commissioner of India?
o: Shankar Singh
Wajahat Habibullah
Nikhil Dey
Aruna Roy
accepted.x: Wajahat Habibullah was the first Central Information Commissioner. Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh were associated with the MKSS movement.
accepted.tq: Separate the first office-holder from activists associated with the RTI movement.
accepted.sec: Central/State Information Commission - composition, appointment, removal, penalty  [APPSC]
